title: Get to Know Each Other
subtitle: 「彼此認識」，究竟是哪一種「互相熟悉」？
description: 「彼此認識」，究竟是哪一種「互相熟悉」？

words.note: 最直接、較正式的近義說法之一，表示兩個人或一群人開始互相認識。
words.example: The workshop gave new staff a chance to become acquainted.
words.exampleZh: 工作坊讓新員工有機會互相認識。

exercises.original: The orientation session helped new employees get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 迎新活動幫助新員工彼此認識。
exercises.upgrade: become acquainted · 認識彼此；開始熟悉

options.explanation: meet = 他們可能早已在 session 開始時見面；這裡重點是開始熟悉。
make friends = 不一定發展到友誼。
become acquainted = orientation 的目的之一是讓新員工開始互相認識，因此 become acquainted 很自然。
socialise = 活動可能包含社交，但句子重點是彼此認識。
know = know 表示已經認識，不突出開始建立熟悉感。
introduce = 介紹只是第一步。

exercises.original: The conference dinner gave delegates time to get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 會議晚宴讓代表有時間彼此認識。
exercises.upgrade: become acquainted · 認識彼此；開始熟悉

options.explanation: meet = 代表可能在白天已見過面，晚宴重點是進一步熟悉。
socialise = 可以，但不能完整表達彼此認識的結果。
make friends = 語義過強。
become acquainted = 晚宴提供較輕鬆時間讓 delegates 開始熟悉，因此 become acquainted 最貼切。
know = 缺少逐步認識過程。
introduce = 不是單次介紹動作。

exercises.original: The first week of training allowed the group to get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 培訓第一星期讓整個小組彼此認識。
exercises.upgrade: become acquainted · 認識彼此；開始熟悉

options.explanation: meet = 一週過程遠超過單純見面。
make friends = 未必成為朋友。
socialise = 只是其中一種方式。
know = 不合動態過程。
become acquainted = 一整週培訓讓小組由陌生逐步變熟，become acquainted 很精確。
introduce = 不是持續一週的活動。

words.note: 描述性說法，強調透過相處和交流逐步變得熟悉。
words.example: Regular team activities help colleagues build familiarity with one another.
words.exampleZh: 定期團隊活動有助同事逐步熟悉彼此。

exercises.original: Working on small tasks together helped the students get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 一起完成小任務幫助學生逐步熟悉彼此。
exercises.upgrade: build familiarity with one another · 建立彼此熟悉感

options.explanation: meet one another = 他們不只是首次見面，而是在合作中逐步熟悉。
make friends = 未必形成友誼。
socialise = 合作任務不一定是社交活動。
build familiarity with one another = 透過共同任務逐步增加熟悉程度，最適合 build familiarity with one another。
introduce themselves = 只是一開始的自我介紹。
know one another = 不突出熟悉感逐步建立。

exercises.original: Regular video calls helped the remote team get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 定期視像會議幫助遙距團隊逐步熟悉彼此。
exercises.upgrade: build familiarity with one another · 建立彼此熟悉感

options.explanation: meet = remote team 可能早已正式見過。
socialise = video calls 未必是純社交。
make friends = 太強。
introduce = 一次介紹不能解釋 regular calls 的作用。
build familiarity with one another = regular calls 表示熟悉感隨時間累積，因此 build familiarity 最自然。
know = 缺少逐步累積。

exercises.original: The shared project gave the two groups a chance to get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 共同項目讓兩組人有機會建立彼此熟悉感。
exercises.upgrade: build familiarity with one another · 建立彼此熟悉感

options.explanation: meet = 共同 project 的作用超過單次見面。
make friends = 不是必要結果。
socialise = 項目合作不等於社交。
know = 不突出發展過程。
introduce = 不合整個 project。
build familiarity with one another = 長期合作讓兩組逐步變熟，因此這個描述性說法很合適。

words.note: 較自然、常見，尤其用於初次見面或剛開始建立關係的情況。
words.example: We had coffee after the meeting so we could get acquainted.
words.exampleZh: 會議後我們一起喝咖啡，好讓彼此認識。

exercises.original: We stayed after the workshop to get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 工作坊後我們留下來彼此認識。
exercises.upgrade: get acquainted · 互相認識；開始熟絡

options.explanation: meet = 大家在 workshop 已經見面。
make friends = 目的未必是建立友誼。
socialise = 可以社交，但句子重點是變得熟悉。
know = 不合逐步過程。
get acquainted = 初次接觸後留下來進一步認識彼此，get acquainted 很自然。
introduce = 不只是交換姓名。

exercises.original: The host arranged a short activity so the guests could get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 主人安排短活動，讓賓客互相認識。
exercises.upgrade: get acquainted · 互相認識；開始熟絡

options.explanation: meet = 活動不只是讓客人第一次碰面。
socialise = 較廣。
make friends = 太強。
know = 不合。
introduce = 如果只是介紹，無需整個 activity。
get acquainted = 讓一群剛認識的 guests 開始熟絡，常用 get acquainted。

exercises.original: The new neighbours invited us for coffee so we could get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 新鄰居邀請我們喝咖啡，好讓彼此認識。
exercises.upgrade: get acquainted · 互相認識；開始熟絡

options.explanation: get acquainted = 喝咖啡是為了從陌生變熟，因此 get acquainted 最貼切。
meet = 鄰居既已邀請，通常已見過面。
make friends = 可能之後會，但不是句子必然結果。
socialise = 喝咖啡是方式，不是核心結果。
know = 不合動態過程。
introduce = 不只是姓名介紹。

words.note: 較中性，強調隨著接觸增加，彼此的性格、習慣或工作方式逐漸變得熟悉。
words.example: The new roommates quickly became familiar with each other's routines.
words.exampleZh: 新室友很快便熟悉彼此的生活習慣。

exercises.original: After living together for a month, the roommates began to get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 同住一個月後，室友開始熟悉彼此。
exercises.upgrade: become familiar with each other · 變得熟悉彼此

options.explanation: meet = 他們已同住一個月，不是首次見面。
make friends = 熟悉彼此不一定變成好友。
introduce themselves = 已經太遲。
socialise = 不一定是社交。
know = 不突出逐步熟悉。
become familiar with each other = 同住讓彼此對 routines 和 habits 逐步熟悉，因此 become familiar with each other 最準確。

exercises.original: The two departments needed time to get to know each other before the merger.
exercises.zh: 合併前，兩個部門需要時間熟悉彼此。
exercises.upgrade: become familiar with each other · 變得熟悉彼此

options.explanation: become familiar with each other = 合併前需要逐步了解彼此工作方式，因此這個說法很自然。
meet = 組織層面不只是見面。
make friends = 不合部門關係。
socialise = 不一定適合正式整合。
introduce = 不夠。
know = 不突出 change over time。

exercises.original: The children became less shy as they got to know each other.
exercises.zh: 孩子們隨著彼此熟悉而變得沒那麼害羞。
exercises.upgrade: become familiar with each other · 變得熟悉彼此

options.explanation: met = 單次見面不能解釋逐漸 less shy。
become familiar with each other = became less shy 表示熟悉度增加，因此 became familiar with each other 很合適。
made friends = 可能發生，但不是唯一原因。
socialised = 描述活動，不如熟悉感自然。
introduced themselves = 太短暫。
knew = 時態和動態意味較弱。

words.note: 和原短語幾乎相同，只是用 one another，常用於群體或較書面語境。
words.example: The retreat gave team members time to get to know one another.
words.exampleZh: 這次團隊活動讓成員有時間彼此認識。

exercises.original: The retreat gave the team time to get to know each other outside work.
exercises.zh: 團隊活動讓成員有時間在工作以外彼此認識。
exercises.upgrade: get to know one another · 彼此認識；互相了解

options.explanation: get to know one another = one another 是群體語境中自然的同義結構，完整保留原意。
meet one another = 成員可能本來已經共事。
make friends = 不一定成為朋友。
socialise = 是方式之一，但不是完整結果。
introduce one another = 不是互相了解。
know one another = 缺少逐步過程。

exercises.original: The course starts with activities that help participants get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 課程以幫助參加者彼此認識的活動開始。
exercises.upgrade: get to know one another · 彼此認識；互相了解

options.explanation: meet = 參加者可能已在報到時見面。
get to know one another = 群體 participants 互相認識時，one another 非常自然。
make friends = 語義過強。
socialise = 較泛。
introduce = 只是初步步驟。
know = 不合。

exercises.original: Team members were encouraged to get to know each other before starting the project.
exercises.zh: 團隊成員被鼓勵在項目開始前彼此認識。
exercises.upgrade: get to know one another · 彼此認識；互相了解

options.explanation: meet = 不只是見一面。
make friends = 不是必需。
get to know one another = 這是最接近原短語的自然變體，尤其適合 group context。
socialise = 可幫助但不是同義。
introduce = 不夠深入。
know = 不突出逐步熟悉。

words.note: 表示彼此已經認識，但希望進一步加深了解。
words.example: The project gave the two departments a chance to become better acquainted.
words.exampleZh: 這個項目讓兩個部門有機會進一步熟悉彼此。

exercises.original: The joint workshop helped the two teams get to know each other better.
exercises.zh: 聯合工作坊幫助兩個團隊進一步熟悉彼此。
exercises.upgrade: become better acquainted · 更加熟悉；進一步認識

options.explanation: meet = 兩個 teams 通常已知道彼此存在。
become better acquainted = better 表示原本已有接觸，現在加深熟悉，因此 become better acquainted 最自然。
make friends = 不合組織語境。
introduce = 只適合初次介紹。
socialise = 活動方式不等於最終熟悉程度。
know = 不如 better acquainted 精確表達進一步認識。

exercises.original: Several meetings allowed the new partners to get to know each other better.
exercises.zh: 數次會面讓新的合作伙伴更加熟悉彼此。
exercises.upgrade: become better acquainted · 更加熟悉；進一步認識

options.explanation: meet = several meetings 已超過單次見面。
make friends = 商業 partners 不一定成為朋友。
become better acquainted = 多次 meetings 讓彼此熟悉程度增加，better acquainted 很精確。
introduce = 第一次 meeting 後已完成。
socialise = 未必是純社交。
know = 缺少比較級加深意味。

exercises.original: The exchange programme helped students from the two schools get to know each other better.
exercises.zh: 交流計劃幫助兩校學生進一步熟悉彼此。
exercises.upgrade: become better acquainted · 更加熟悉；進一步認識

options.explanation: meet = exchange programme 目的更深入。
make friends = 可能發生但不是必要。
socialise = 只是其中一環。
become better acquainted = 交流計劃讓已有初步接觸的學生加深認識，因此這個說法最貼切。
introduce = 不夠。
know = 不如 become better acquainted 表達發展過程。

words.note: 強調知道對方的背景、興趣、經驗或想法，語義比單純『認識』更偏向實際了解。
words.example: The students shared short introductions to learn about each other.
words.exampleZh: 學生透過簡短自我介紹來了解彼此。

exercises.original: The students shared short introductions to get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 學生透過簡短自我介紹來了解彼此。
exercises.upgrade: learn about each other · 了解彼此

options.explanation: meet = 自我介紹後不只是見面。
make friends = 未必。
learn about each other = short introductions 提供彼此背景資訊，因此 learn about each other 最精確。
socialise = introductions 可屬社交，但重點是了解背景。
know = 不突出取得新資訊。
acquaint = 結構不自然。

exercises.original: The activity asked participants to discuss their interests so they could get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 活動要求參加者談自己的興趣，好讓彼此了解。
exercises.upgrade: learn about each other · 了解彼此

options.explanation: meet = 大家已在 activity 中見面。
make friends = 目的未必是友誼。
socialise = 太泛。
learn about each other = 談 interests 的目的就是獲得對方資訊，因此 learn about each other 很自然。
know = 不如 learn about 突出資訊內容。
introduce = 不只是交換姓名。

exercises.original: We asked questions about work and hobbies to get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 我們互相詢問工作和興趣，以了解彼此。
exercises.upgrade: learn about each other · 了解彼此

options.explanation: meet = 不是首次碰面。
socialise = 問問題是社交方式，但重點是知道內容。
make friends = 過強。
introduce = 不等於深入詢問。
learn about each other = questions about work and hobbies 直接增加彼此了解，因此這個替換最自然。
know = 不如 learn about 具體。

words.note: 當 get to know each other 不只是認識，而是逐步建立信任和良好互動時，可用 build rapport；語義比原短語稍強。
words.example: The opening activity helped the participants build rapport.
words.exampleZh: 開場活動幫助參加者建立融洽關係。

exercises.original: The team-building exercise helped the new staff get to know each other and feel more comfortable together.
exercises.zh: 團隊活動幫助新員工彼此認識，並建立更自在的互動。
exercises.upgrade: build rapport · 建立融洽關係

options.explanation: meet = 他們可能已見過面，而且 feel more comfortable 表示關係進一步改善。
introduce = 只是一開始。
know = 不突出關係品質。
build rapport = feel more comfortable together 顯示不只是熟悉，而是建立融洽感，因此 build rapport 最精確。
make friends = 比 rapport 更強、更私人。
socialise = 不一定帶來互相信任。

exercises.original: The facilitator used pair activities to help participants get to know each other before discussion.
exercises.zh: 帶領者用二人活動幫助參加者在討論前建立融洽感。
exercises.upgrade: build rapport · 建立融洽關係

options.explanation: meet = pair activity 目的不只是見面。
introduce = 不夠深入。
socialise = 可描述活動，但不是關係成果。
make friends = 過強。
build rapport = pair activities 常用來讓 participants 建立互信和自然互動，因此 build rapport 很合適。
know = 不突出互動舒適度。

exercises.original: The informal lunch helped the two managers get to know each other before negotiations began.
exercises.zh: 非正式午餐幫助兩名經理在談判前建立融洽關係。
exercises.upgrade: build rapport · 建立融洽關係

options.explanation: meet = 他們可能早已知道彼此身份。
make friends = 商業語境過強。
introduce = 不合 informal lunch 的深入交流。
know = 缺少關係品質。
socialise = 是方式而不是結果。
build rapport = 談判前透過 informal lunch 建立良好互動關係，build rapport 最自然。

words.note: 較正式，強調雙方透過持續接觸逐步形成相互熟悉。
words.example: Repeated collaboration helped the two teams develop mutual familiarity.
words.exampleZh: 反覆合作幫助兩個團隊建立彼此熟悉感。

exercises.original: Repeated collaboration helped the two teams get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 反覆合作幫助兩個團隊建立彼此熟悉感。
exercises.upgrade: develop mutual familiarity · 建立彼此熟悉感

options.explanation: meet = 多次 collaboration 遠超過見面。
make friends = 不合團隊關係。
introduce = 不是一次性介紹。
socialise = 合作不等於社交。
develop mutual familiarity = repeated collaboration 表示熟悉感累積，因此正式說法 develop mutual familiarity 很貼切。
know = 不突出熟悉程度逐步形成。

exercises.original: Working side by side for several months allowed staff to get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 一起工作數月讓員工建立彼此熟悉感。
exercises.upgrade: develop mutual familiarity · 建立彼此熟悉感

options.explanation: meet = 早已超過初次見面。
make friends = 未必形成私人友誼。
socialise = 不是重點。
introduce = 不合數月過程。
know = 不如 develop familiarity 強調變化。
develop mutual familiarity = 數月共同工作逐步形成雙向熟悉，develop mutual familiarity 很精確。

exercises.original: The regular meetings helped members of both committees get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 定期會議幫助兩個委員會的成員彼此熟悉。
exercises.upgrade: develop mutual familiarity · 建立彼此熟悉感

options.explanation: develop mutual familiarity = regular contact 建立雙方熟悉程度，因此這個正式表達很自然。
meet = regular meetings 說明不只是初見。
make friends = 不是委員會合作必要結果。
introduce = 早期已完成。
socialise = 會議未必是社交。
know = 不突出 gradual development。

words.word: Become more familiar with one another
words.note: 表示在已有初步接觸的基礎上，進一步了解對方。
words.example: Working together for several weeks helped them become more familiar with one another.
words.exampleZh: 一起工作數星期後，他們彼此更加熟悉。

exercises.original: After several group sessions, the participants began to get to know each other better.
exercises.zh: 數次小組活動後，參加者開始更加熟悉彼此。
exercises.upgrade: become more familiar with one another · 彼此更加熟悉
exercises.answer: become more familiar with one another

options.explanation: meet = 已經有 several sessions。
make friends = 未必。
introduce = 不合。
socialise = 只是可能的方式。
know = 不如 more familiar 表達程度增加。

options.text: become more familiar with one another
options.explanation: become more familiar with one another = several group sessions 令熟悉程度加深，因此 become more familiar with one another 合適。

exercises.original: The shared office helped colleagues get to know each other better over time.
exercises.zh: 共用辦公室令同事隨時間更加熟悉彼此。
exercises.upgrade: become more familiar with one another · 彼此更加熟悉
exercises.answer: become more familiar with one another

options.text: become more familiar with one another
options.explanation: become more familiar with one another = over time 是漸進熟悉的明確線索，因此這個說法很自然。
meet = 同事本來已見面。
make friends = 未必。
socialise = 不一定。
introduce = 不合 over time。
know = 不突出程度改變。

exercises.original: Training together helped the two groups get to know each other better.
exercises.zh: 一起培訓幫助兩組人更加熟悉彼此。
exercises.upgrade: become more familiar with one another · 彼此更加熟悉
exercises.answer: become more familiar with one another

options.explanation: meet = 不只是見面。

options.text: become more familiar with one another
options.explanation: become more familiar with one another = 共同 training 令彼此熟悉程度增加，因此這個替換完整保留原意。
make friends = 不是必要。
introduce = 不夠。
socialise = 不是唯一作用。
know = 不如 more familiar 精確。

words.note: 較口語，表示透過相處逐漸熟悉彼此；通常比 become familiar with each other 更口語。
words.example: The new team spent the first afternoon getting familiar with each other.
words.exampleZh: 新團隊第一個下午用來彼此熟絡。

exercises.original: The new team spent the first afternoon getting to know each other.
exercises.zh: 新團隊第一個下午用來彼此熟絡。
exercises.upgrade: get familiar with each other · 彼此熟絡；互相熟悉

options.explanation: get familiar with each other = 新團隊初期由陌生到熟悉，較口語可說 getting familiar with each other。
meeting = 第一次下午可能有見面，但整個 afternoon 用於熟悉彼此。
making friends = 過強。
socialising = 也可能，但重點是變熟。
introducing = 太短暫。
knowing = 語法和動態意味都不合。

exercises.original: The roommates used the first few days to get to know each other.
exercises.zh: 室友用最初幾天來彼此熟絡。
exercises.upgrade: get familiar with each other · 彼此熟絡；互相熟悉

options.explanation: meet = 他們第一天已會見面。
get familiar with each other = first few days 表示逐步熟絡，因此這個較口語說法可自然使用。
make friends = 未必成為朋友。
introduce themselves = 不會花 several days。
socialise = 可以，但不完整。
know = 不合漸進過程。

exercises.original: The volunteers had lunch together to get to know each other before the event.
exercises.zh: 義工在活動前一起吃午飯，以彼此熟絡。
exercises.upgrade: get familiar with each other · 彼此熟絡；互相熟悉

options.explanation: meet = 吃 lunch 目的不只是見面。
make friends = 未必。
get familiar with each other = 活動前透過 lunch 令彼此不再陌生，get familiar with each other 很自然。
introduce = 只是一開始。
socialise = 是方式之一。
know = 不突出逐步熟悉。

falseSynonyms.zh: 見面不等於互相了解 meet 只表示首次或某次見面；get to know each other 強調見面後逐步了解彼此。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON People can meet once without getting to know each other well.

falseSynonyms.zh: 介紹不等於互相認識 introduce 是讓彼此知道姓名或身份；它只是開始認識的一個步驟。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON An introduction may help people begin to get to know each other.

falseSynonyms.zh: 知道／認識不等於逐步認識 know 表示已經認識或知道；get to know 強調從不熟悉到逐步熟悉的過程。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON I know her now because I spent time getting to know her.

falseSynonyms.zh: 交朋友比互相認識更強 make friends 表示建立友誼；人們可以 get to know each other 而不一定成為朋友。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Colleagues may get to know each other without becoming close friends.

falseSynonyms.zh: 社交不等於互相了解 socialise 表示和別人交往或參與社交活動；它可能促進認識，但不是同一概念。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Socialising can help people get to know each other.

falseSynonyms.zh: 動態過程與狀態不同 get to know 表示逐步認識；know 表示已經認識或了解。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON They are getting to know each other. They already know each other quite well.

falseSynonyms.zh: 動詞與狀態不同 acquaint 是使某人熟悉；acquainted 表示已經認識或熟悉。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON The event acquainted staff with the new system. The staff became acquainted with one another.

falseSynonyms.zh: 關係融洽與熟悉程度不同 rapport 強調信任和良好互動；familiarity 只表示熟悉，未必有親近感。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON People can be familiar with each other without having strong rapport.
